prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1070; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'm sorry, I'd rather not put my name on this recording yet. Can you just refer to me as the claimant?

Q: That's fine. For the record, you were the driver of the vehicle involved in the rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas. Is that correct?

A: Yes, I was driving my car. I was stopped at a red light on the main road when it happened.

Q: Can you describe what happened just before the impact?

A: I had been stopped for maybe ten or fifteen seconds. Then I felt a hard jolt from behind. The car lurched forward and my head snapped back and then forward again.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was belted in.

Q: Did the other driver say anything at the scene?

A: They apologized right away. They said they looked down at their phone for a second and didn't brake in time.

Q: Did you seek medical attention after the accident?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon. They told me I had neck and back strain.

Q: How are you feeling now?

A: My neck is still stiff, especially when I turn to check my blind spot. My lower back aches when I sit for long periods. I've been doing the exercises the doctor gave me, and I'm trying to keep up with physical therapy.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injuries?

A: A few days, yes. I'm able to do light duty now, but lifting and long shifts are still hard.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know?

A: Just that I have photos of the vehicles and the intersection, and I'm willing to share them. I'd like this claim handled as quickly as possible.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
